jobs.description:
Why Hershey:

At The Hershey Company, our culture is rooted in purpose and inspired by Milton Hershey’s enduring vision that business should create opportunity for others. Through our commitment to corporate philanthropy, we create positive impact by supporting communities, helping children thrive, and operating as a business for good. This includes our deep and long standing partnership with Milton Hershey School, where we invest in education, workforce readiness, and hands on engagement to help students succeed beyond the classroom. Supported by strategic grantmaking, product donations, cross brand collaboration, and strong employee volunteerism, Hershey offers a place to work where making a difference—locally and globally—is part of how we do business every day.

Location: Hershey, PA

This role is based in Hershey, PA with an expectation of 3 days per week in the Hershey office.

About The Hershey Company

The Hershey Company (NYSE: HSY) is an industry-leading snacks company known for making more moments of goodness through its iconic brands. With a strong portfolio across chocolate, confectionery, and salty snacks, Hershey delights consumers every day. Our beloved brands include Hershey’s, Reese’s, KitKat®, Dots Pretzels, Lesser Evil, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Ice Breakers, and more.
At Hershey, we are committed to making a meaningful difference in the communities where we live, work, and do business. This commitment originated with our founder, Milton Hershey, and continues to shape who we are today.
Guided by our employee value proposition, Lead Today. Create Tomorrow, we empower our people to drive impact now while shaping what comes next. Our One Hershey mindset brings teams together across functions, geographies, and businesses, enabling us to operate with speed, collaboration, and shared purpose.
The Hershey Company is proud to be recognized as a top employer in the United States, reflecting our commitment to our people, culture, and purpose

How will you fit in the big picture?

The U.S. business is at the center of delivering this vision, navigating an increasingly dynamic environment shaped by evolving consumer preferences, changing customer expectations, competitive disruption, economic uncertainty, and an accelerating pace of transformation.

The Chief of Staff to the President, U.S. serves as a trusted advisor, strategic thought partner, and force multiplier to the President and the U.S. Leadership Team (USLT). This highly visible leadership role bridges strategy and execution by helping shape business priorities, driving enterprise alignment, accelerating strategic initiatives, and maximizing organizational effectiveness across the U.S. business.

As the President's right hand, the Chief of Staff enables faster, better decision-making; optimizes operating rhythms, governance, and resource allocation; and ensures the successful execution of the U.S. growth agenda. This leader serves as an enterprise connector who brings together cross-functional teams to solve complex business challenges, drive transformational initiatives, and deliver measurable business results.

What will you do?

Strategic Leadership & Enterprise Planning

- Serve as a strategic advisor to the President, U.S., providing insight on growth, performance, transformation, and organizational effectiveness.

- Lead annual and long-range strategic planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and value creation goals.

- Leverage consumer, customer, competitive, and market intelligence to identify risks and growth opportunities.

- Support executive decision-making through business cases, scenario planning, financial analysis, and recommendations.

- Lead strategic projects, transformation initiatives, and evaluations of growth, innovation, and M&A opportunities.

Leadership Team Effectiveness & Governance

- Drive the effectiveness of the U.S. Leadership Team through governance, operating rhythms, decision frameworks, and accountability processes.

- Facilitate key business reviews, planning sessions, and leadership meetings.

- Align leaders around priorities, decisions, and execution.

- Represent the President when appropriate to advance business priorities and decisions.

- Improve the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.

Strategic Initiative & Program Leadership

- Lead execution of the President's highest-priority initiatives and ensure delivery of measurable business outcomes.

- Manage cross-functional programs, governance structures, milestones, and accountability.

- Proactively mitigate risks, remove obstacles, and resolve dependencies.

- Coordinate enterprise initiatives across Commercial, Marketing, Supply Chain, Finance, HR, Digital, and other functions.

- Advise USLT members on critical business initiatives and strategic opportunities.

Commercial Excellence & Business Performance

- Monitor business performance and key metrics, providing actionable recommendations to the President and USLT.

- Assess business risks and opportunities and partner with leaders to develop action plans.

- Ensure alignment among strategic priorities, investments, resources, and execution.

- Support delivery of Annual Operating Plan commitments and long-term growth objectives.

- Identify opportunities to strengthen competitive advantage through innovation, partnerships, digital capabilities, and portfolio expansion.

Operating Model

- Own and continuously improve the U.S. operating model, enabling effective governance, planning, communication, and decision-making.

- Integrate priorities into quarterly, annual, and strategic planning processes.

- Maintain focus on the most critical enterprise objectives.

- Drive OKR governance, measurement, and accountability.

- Improve cross-functional coordination and organizational execution.

Executive Communications & Stakeholder Engagement

- Develop executive communications, presentations, and strategic narratives for leadership, Board, investor, and external audiences.

- Partner with Corporate Communications and business leaders to ensure consistent messaging.

- Prepare the President for internal and external engagements, including Board meetings, town halls, customer interactions, and industry events.

- Serve as a communication bridge between the President, USLT, and broader organization.

- Partner with the Executive Assistant to maximize the President's effectiveness and focus.

Minimum Requirements

Education

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Marketing, Organizational Leadership, Analytics, or a related field required.

- MBA or other advanced degree strongly preferred .

Experience

The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of progressive leadership experience across strategy, consulting, commercial leadership, business operations, corporate development, transformation, or executive advisory roles.

Preferred experience includes:

- Chief of Staff, strategy, consulting, business operations, or commercial leadership experience.

- Experience working directly with senior executives and leadership teams.

- Background in consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, retail, or related growth-oriented industries.

- Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives from strategy development through execution.

- Exposure to M&A, portfolio strategy, innovation, business model transformation, or enterprise change initiatives.

- Proven success influencing senior stakeholders and leading without formal authority.

- Demonstrated track record developing executive-level and Board-ready materials and communications.

How Will You Fit in the Big Picture?

The Manager, Continuous Improvement will help create a zero-loss culture across assigned manufacturing operations by developing and implementing process improvements, strengthening operator capability, and improving the consistency and quality of service and execution. This role manages teams within a defined discipline and translates business priorities into tactical and operational plans that address cross-team issues, reduce rework, and improve performance.

As a leader in Hershey Lean, this manager will guide process mapping, workflow redesign, daily management systems, and data-driven problem solving. The role will support the implementation of Redzone and related standards, maintain visibility to line-loss data, and lead continuous improvement projects from ideation through execution. Success requires practical judgment, strong stakeholder partnership, and the ability to solve difficult or undefined problems through data analysis and corrective action

What Will You Do?

- Lead teams responsible for day-to-day process execution, service delivery, and continuous improvement within an assigned manufacturing area.

- Set clear goals, roles, decision rights, performance expectations, and accountability for team members.

- Review performance against established metrics and standards, identify gaps, and implement corrective actions that improve service quality and operational consistency.

- Drive daily problem solving and data-driven planning for targeted manufacturing operations, using line-loss data to prioritize the most significant opportunities.

- Coach plant leadership and front-line teams on daily management systems and execution standards using Redzone, S/4, Hershey Lean, and associated tools and practices.

- Develop and implement improvements from loss diagnostics and ideation through process changes and capital projects.

- Coordinate process mapping and workflow redesign across teams, ensuring solutions are practical and aligned with customer and stakeholder needs.

- Support financial valuation for the continuous improvement pipeline, capital projects, new item costing, and related initiatives.

- Partner with stakeholders to clarify service delivery requirements, manage expectations, resolve cross-team issues, and sustain improvements.

- Establish training programs for front-line operators on Hershey Lean standards and build team capability through coaching, feedback, and development.

- Promote alignment across sites by sharing standards, practices, and continuous improvement learnings.

Minimum Requirements

Experience:

- 5+ years of relevant experience.

- Experience working in an automated manufacturing environment preferred.

- Demonstrated experience leading teams and driving process, system, or operational improvements.

- Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Lean Six Sigma tools, and Total Productive Maintenance preferred.

- Experience developing and facilitating training programs preferred.

- Experience collecting, analyzing, and translating data into practical action plans.

- Demonstrated change management, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

- Ability to work independently, take ownership, and address complex or undefined operational problems.

- Experience with Redzone, OSI PI, Power Apps, Power BI, Microsoft 365, or similar digital manufacturing and analytics tools preferred.

- Ability to travel up to 25%.

Education:

- Bachelor's degree required.

2.     Portfolio Strategy & Growth Stewardship: Shape the future of the portfolio by identifying where to play and how to win, optimizing brands, products, and channels to maximize consumer relevance, commercial impact, and long-term value creation.

Drive Customer Points of Sale through Consultative Business Partnering

Qualifications

How Will You Fit in the Big Picture?

The Territory Sales Lead (TSL) ensures flawless execution of store level sales and promotion plans with customer retailers in assigned territory.  The territory consists of high-volume food chain grocers and mass merchandiser customers.  The TSL masters retail execution plans by driving incremental sales, implementing, and maintaining best-in-class promotional and merchandising strategies, and ensuring 100% distribution on authorized Hershey items across all classes of trade (Grocery, Mass Merch, Drug & Convenience). A successful TSL will be driven, entrepreneurial, influential, and planful.

What Will You Do?

Consultative Business Partnering
Customer Relationship Development and Management:

- Build and maintain consultative business relationships with customer Key Decision Makers (KDMs) at all levels.

- Partner and collaborate with KDMs to develop and execute action plans to increase sales. Cultivate a network of influential contacts at all levels of customers to achieve sales objectives.

- Leverage strategic relationships with KDMs to influence and negotiate customers’ assistance in the merchandising of Hershey products.

Data Analysis:

- Obtain and analyze relevant store, product, and market data and leverage trends and analytics to build the business.

- Utilize and complete pre-call planning methods and other company tools.

- Review and make recommendations to modify routes that maximize business efficiencies for all sales calls within territory.

- Effectively solve problems by analyzing information, utilizing consumer trends and customer insights to guide decision making and influence others to act.

Sales:

- Engage in forward selling via consultative sales techniques using provided data sources, technology, processes and procedures.

- Maximize sales and display opportunities by conducting store walk-throughs and gaining commitment by KDMs on successful outcomes.

- Tailor strategies to influence KDMs to order additional products to increase incremental sales and to obtain best in class quality of merchandising locations.

- Advocacy Roles for an identified Banner – will be required to communicate the objectives or changes from the account to your colleagues

Merchandising
Achieve all merchandising objectives executing customer specific promotional plans to the sales floor using forward selling. Partnership at store level is critical for TSL’s to effectively build, maintain and execute product on the sales floor, in addition to merchandising and maintaining permanent secondary displays and other display vehicles as well as identifying out of stocks.

Administrative Responsibilities
Complete and submit reports of daily and weekly activities, expenses, competitive activity, viva engage posts (photos of displays), account changes, promotions and all administrative functions within assigned territory using company approved methods and technology

Education and Experience:
•    High School Diploma
•    2-year Associate/Community College degree required OR 3 years of previous sales experience.
•    Bachelor's degree strongly preferred to move to future roles within the organization

Minimum knowledge, skills and abilities required to successfully perform essential duties/responsibilities, with or without a reasonable accommodation:
• Must have a valid Canadian issued driver’s license and good standing record (Driver Abstract report will be required through the background check)
• Must reside or be willing to commute within territory boundaries
• Must be able to drive to make multiple sales calls on a daily basis
• Must be able to lift 30-60 lbs on a regular basis with or without reasonable accommodations.
• Must be able to bend, kneel, stoop down and demonstrate manual dexterity on a frequent basis with or without reasonable accommodations
• Occasionally climb ladders & use step stools
• Occasionally use equipment such as crushing balers, handheld electric trucks or flatbed carts working inventory in the backrooms
• Must be able to use tablet, IPad  and other wireless technology; some roles will require an intermediate level of computer skills with the Microsoft Office products (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Co-pilot)
• Must have daily access to wireless internet
• Must have flexibility and adaptability to changes in territory coverage
• Occasional weekend work may be required during peak seasons and select territories may require occasional overnight stays.

jobs.description:
Location - Mississauga, ON

About the Hershey Company

The Hershey Company (NYSE: HSY) is an industry-leading snacks company known for making more moments of goodness through its iconic brands. With a strong portfolio across chocolate, confectionery, and salty snacks, Hershey delights consumers every day. Our beloved brands include Hershey’s, Reese’s, KitKat®, Dots Pretzels, Lesser Evil, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Ice Breakers, and more.

At Hershey, we are committed to making a meaningful difference in the communities where we live, work, and do business. This commitment originated with our founder, Milton Hershey, and continues to shape who we are today.

Guided by our employee value proposition, Lead Today. Create Tomorrow, we empower our people to drive impact now while shaping what comes next. Our One Hershey mindset brings teams together across functions, geographies, and businesses, enabling us to operate with speed, collaboration, and shared purpose.

The Hershey Company is proud to be recognized as a top employer in the United States, reflecting our commitment to our people, culture, and purpose.

How Will You Fit in the Big Picture?

Reporting to the Marketing Finance Manager, the Associate Manager, Marketing Finance is accountable for providing financial leadership for a portfolio of chocolate, sweets, and seasons brands. This role partners closely with the business to evaluate investments, assess performance, identify risks and opportunities, and influence decisions that advance Hershey Canada's growth and profitability objectives. By combining strategic thinking, financial insight, and strong business partnership, the Associate Manager helps optimize portfolio performance and deliver sustainable profitable growth.

What Will You Do?

- Innovation and Strategic Investments : Lead the monthly innovation business-case financials partnering with Marketing, Sales Finance and Revenue Management. Rigorously assess financial inputs, assumptions, risks and opportunities, and deliver clear recommendations that influence stakeholders and drive profitable investment decisions.

- Brand P&L and Performance : Partner with marketers to strengthen brand health and improve brand P&L performance. Establish performance guardrails, evaluate price, mix and promotional strategies, identify risks and opportunities, and provide actionable insights that support profitable, sustainable brand decisions.

- Business Partnership : Deliver actionable financial information to Marketing leaders and teams at all levels, translating performance drivers into clear decisions and actions. Build business acumen through regular coaching, influence stakeholders on investment choices, and support monthly and quarterly business reviews.

- Budgeting, Forecasting and Analysis : Lead the execution of the end-to-end Canada division expense budgeting and forecasting processes, partnering with stakeholders to develop and validate assumptions, improve forecast accuracy, and identify risks and opportunities for the country forecast. Perform monthly variance analysis of actual results against plan and prior year and provide clear, actionable recommendations.

- Financial Reporting and Controls : Support the Marketing Finance Manager with monthly financial analysis and reporting for marketing expenses and COGS. Develop sustainable reports and tools, review the end-to-end reporting structure, and streamline current processes to provide timely insights that help the Marketing team make profitable business decisions.

- Deliver high-quality ad hoc analysis related to COGS, division expense and brand profitability. Translate multiple data sources into clear insights and recommendations.

- Develop strong relationships across all levels of Hershey Canada and identify opportunities to continuously improve business performance and ways of working.

- Drive transparency by developing and maintaining models, analytical tools and processes that help cross-functional partners make profitable business decisions.

Minimum Education & Requirements

•Minimum 3–5 years of progressive finance experience in the CPG sector or a similar fast-paced, consumer-focused industry. Commercial finance experience is preferred.
•Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or Business; MBA or CPA preferred, or equivalent relevant experience.

•Strong business contributor who consistently demonstrates strategic thinking, analytical capability and leadership.
•Effective communicator who can build strong relationships and influence all levels of the organization.
•Ability to independently arrive at insights and develop creative solutions to solve complex business problems. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional projects.
•Proactive self-starter who challenges the status quo and continuously seeks improvement.
•Ability to prioritize and manage multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.
•Solid understanding of financial metrics and P&L fundamentals.
•Fluency with Excel, and PowerPoint are critical. Knowledge of PowerBl and Alteryx is a plus but not compulsory.

- Manage key HR processes, including HRIS/SAP data entry and reporting, attendance and leave tracking, and coordination of disciplinary actions.

- Support employee engagement initiatives and organizational change efforts.

- Analyze turnover, attrition, and other key HR metrics to identify trends and recommend actionable solutions to HR and plant leadership.

- Apply knowledge of the business to support effective decision-making, consistent HR processes, and organizational performance.

- Identify opportunities to simplify processes, remove barriers, reduce costs, and improve HR service delivery.

- Leverage HR technology, shared services, and available resources to effectively meet employee and business needs.

- Support wage surveys and market-competitive compensation recommendations.

- 3–5 years of Human Resources experience, including at least 1 year in a leadership capacity.

- Working knowledge and practical application of federal and state employment laws.

- Experience with employee/labor relations, recruitment and selection, compensation and benefits, and HR policy interpretation.

- Experience administering FMLA, workers’ compensation, and unemployment processes.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills with the ability to translate data into actionable recommendations.

- Demonstrated ability to lead projects, manage competing priorities, and collaborate across levels and functions in a matrixed organization.

- Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to facilitate learning with large groups.

- Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams, along with experience working with HRIS systems.
